correctness.rationale: Unary rank-r types consist of first r vertices, last r vertices and an interior class once n>=2r+2; the two-variable quantifier recurrence checks equality, predecessor, successor and nonadjacent occurrence. Closed q-sentences depend on realized rank-(q-1) unary types. The explicit Theta_{a,b} with a+b=t-5 yields each t from 3 to 2q-1 at depth <=q; rank-two formulas isolate t=1,2. Fresh rank-refinement computations over lengths 1..22 and ranks 1..6 reproduced exactly 1 and 2q classes. This is not a proof by finite enumeration; the induction provides all n.
residual_risks: Finite calculations are not universal proofs; precise proof lemmas assessed separately.

originality.rationale: Weis and Immerman 2009 Theorem 21 already characterizes rank-q FO2[<,Suc] equivalence on all words by successor-ranker occurrence and successor-order patterns. On one-letter words these stabilize beyond 2q endpoint positions; forgetting < gives the exact claimed long-path FO2[S] collapse, and the remaining small-length separations follow by elementary successor-only formulas. Thus the assessed theorem is a routine corollary/specialization of a stronger published structural result. Distinct wording or failure to print 2q as a headline is not originality.
residual_risks: It is not explicitly printed as a 2q corollary in Weis–Immerman; the implication is obtained by one-letter specialization plus elementary FO²[S] separators, not an identical quoted theorem.
No claim that the 2009 paper proves an incorrect 2q result; its stronger theorem controls the upper bound.
